newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Costa Rica leader pledges to support Taiwan UN bid.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica leader pledges to support Taiwan UN bid.

text.p: Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres on Thursday risked provoking China by pledging support for Taiwan's membership in the United Nations.

"We will continue to give our firm support to the Republic of China (Taiwan's official title)," Figueres said in his pre-departure news conference when asked if Costa Rica would back Taiwan U.N. membership.
"Costa Rica has always stood on its 100-year tradition of democracy...to help all those countries the world over to have the rights to participate and be listened to," he said.
Figueres said there is nothing wrong for Taiwan to wish to join international organisation, calling it is a "fair desire".

Figueres, who was to return to Costa Rica later on Thursday after a six-day visit, said his country stands by its belief in democracy and peace, and would not bow to any pressure from China and switch recognition to Beijing.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split the two in 1949, has warned other countries against forging ties with Taipei and supporting the island's bid to join the United Nations.
Costa Rica, Nicaragua and several other Central American countries recently proposed a discussion on granting Taiwan U.N. membership during a General Assembly session in September.
Figueres on Thursday signed a joint communiqu with his local host President Lee Teng-hui, pledging support for each other.
Under the communiqu, Taiwan agreed to cooperate with Costa Rica economically, socially and educationally.
Figueres also invited Taiwanese businessmen to invest in his country.
Costa Rica, in need of foreign investment, is among the 31 diplomatic allies that recognise Taipei instead of Beijing.
That number will be reduced to 30 after South Africa switches diplomatic recognition to Beijing at the end of 1997.
